24 A jet aircraft travels at a speed of 0.80v, where v is the speed of sound. The aircraft directly
approaches a stationary observer. The frequency of sound emitted by the aircraft is 100 Hz.
Which frequency does the observer hear?
A
56 Hz
B
180 Hz
C
400 Hz
D
500 Hz

hints: Notice the source speed $0.80v$ is a large fraction of the wave speed $v$, and the aircraft is directly approaching the stationary observer with emitted frequency 100 Hz.
Recall that for an approaching source the observed wavelength is shortened to $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$, so the observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o$ must be larger than $f_s$.
Write $f_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$, substitute $v_s = 0.80v$ to get $v - 0.80v = 0.20v$, then multiply 100 Hz by $1/0.20$.
walkthrough: Identify the Doppler situation: source speed $v_s = 0.80v$ toward a stationary observer, wave speed $v$, source frequency $f_s = 100 \text{ Hz}$.

State the rule for an approaching source: successive wavefronts are crowded together, so observed wavelength $\lambda_o = (v - v_s)/f_s$ and observed frequency $f_o = v/\lambda_o = f_s \times v/(v - v_s)$.
Calculate: $f_o = 100 \text{ Hz} \times v/(0.20v) = 100 \text{ Hz} \times 5 = 500 \text{ Hz}$ with unit $\text{Hz}$ as expected for frequency.
This large increase makes sense because the source is chasing its own sound waves at 80 percent of the wave speed. This is option D.

A.explanation: 56 Hz is lower than the 100 Hz emitted, but an approaching source compresses wavefronts and must give a higher observed frequency.

B.explanation: 180 Hz uses $v + v_s$ in the denominator instead of $v - v_s$, which applies to a receding source rather than an approaching source.

C.explanation: 400 Hz would result from dividing by 0.25, which miscalculates $1 - 0.80$ as 0.25 instead of 0.20.
